name: receptionist-kb-goldset
description: Goldset for the AI receptionist knowledge base. 45 FAQ chunks and 232 questions (177 single-chunk, 29 multi-chunk, 26 distractor). Questions are hand-written paraphrases in five registers (colloquial, formal, terse, multi-clause, typo-laden) so that lexical keyword matching alone cannot reach full recall. The distractor set is out-of-domain requests a receptionist must refuse rather than answer. IMPORTANT: these are synthetic queries authored against this corpus, NOT real visitor logs. They measure the retrieval policy, not real-world demand.

chunks.title: Opening Hours
chunks.text: Northwind Dental Studio is open Monday to Friday from 9:00am to 5:00pm EST. On Saturdays we open from 10:00am to 2:00pm. We are closed on Sundays and on public holidays. The last appointment of the day starts 30 minutes before closing.

chunks.title: Clinic Location and Parking
chunks.text: The clinic is at 214 Maple Street, Suite 300, Riverton, NY 10019. Visitor parking is free in the garage behind the building; enter from Bell Avenue. Street parking on Maple Street is metered and enforced from 8am to 7pm. The building is fully wheelchair accessible and the elevator is located beside the reception desk.

chunks.title: Booking an Appointment
chunks.text: Appointments can be requested online or by phone. A request is not confirmed until a member of the front desk calls you back, usually within one business day. New patients must provide a date of birth and insurance details before the visit is confirmed. Please arrive 15 minutes early to complete paperwork.

chunks.title: Rescheduling and Cancellations
chunks.text: You can reschedule or cancel without charge up to 24 hours before your appointment. Inside 24 hours the cancellation counts as a no-show and a 50 dollar late cancellation fee applies. To reschedule, call the office or reply to your confirmation email and we will send a new slot.

chunks.title: Insurance and Payment
chunks.text: We are in network with Delta Dental, Cigna and MetLife. For out of network insurance we provide a written estimate but require payment at the time of service. Copays are collected at check-in. We accept Visa, Mastercard, American Express, FSA and HSA cards as well as cash.

chunks.title: Dental Services
chunks.text: Services include routine cleanings, digital X-rays, fillings, crowns, root canals, tooth extractions, teeth whitening, dental implants and emergency treatment for toothaches. Children are welcome and we see patients from age three.

chunks.title: Dental Emergencies
chunks.text: For a dental emergency such as severe pain, swelling, a broken tooth or an injury, call the office immediately and press 1 for the on-call dentist. We reserve same-day slots for emergencies and aim to see you within 24 hours. If your face is swollen and you have difficulty breathing or swallowing, call 911 first.

chunks.title: Teeth Whitening
chunks.text: In office whitening takes about 90 minutes and usually lightens teeth by several shades. Take home kits provide custom trays and gel to use for 30 minutes a day for about two weeks. Whitening is not recommended for people under 18, pregnant visitors, or anyone with untreated cavities.

chunks.title: First Visit for Children
chunks.text: A first child visit is a friendly 20 minute orientation with teeth counting and a quick cleaning. Children should come with a parent or guardian who can provide consent. We ask parents to book early morning slots because children tend to be calmer then. A small reward sticker is given at the end of the visit.

chunks.title: Technology at the Clinic
chunks.text: We use digital X-rays that use 80 percent less radiation than film and produce images on screen in seconds. Intraoral cameras let you see your own teeth on the monitor during the exam. Patient records are stored in a secure encrypted system.

chunks.title: Patient Privacy and Records
chunks.text: We follow HIPAA for all patient data. Records are only released to a patient or a legally authorized representative, and photo identification is required before we hand over copies. Treatment histories older than seven years are archived but remain available on request.

chunks.title: Phone and Email
chunks.text: The office phone is 555 0142 and the fax is 555 0143. Email reception@northwinddental.example and we reply within one business day. Voicemail is monitored between 9:00am and 5:00pm, and messages left after hours are returned the next morning.

chunks.title: First Thing in the Morning
chunks.text: The very first appointment of the day is reserved for emergency and urgent care patients. If you are in pain and need the earliest possible slot, call at 8:30am and we will try to fit you in before the scheduled patients arrive.

chunks.title: Cosmetic Consultations
chunks.text: Cosmetic consultations are free and last about 45 minutes. A dentist will take photographs, discuss veneers and whitening, and produce a written treatment plan with costs. Cosmetic work is never urgent and is scheduled outside emergency slots.

chunks.title: Transferring Records
chunks.text: To transfer records to another dentist, send a written request with your full name and date of birth. We need a signed release form, and the receiving practice usually receives the file within five business days. Digital X-rays are sent on a portable drive.

chunks.title: Dental Implants
chunks.text: A dental implant replaces a missing tooth permanently and is made of titanium. The procedure takes two to three appointments over about four months and is performed by a periodontist or an oral surgeon, not by the general dentist. Implants are not covered by routine insurance and are quoted individually after a CT scan.

chunks.title: Crowns and Bridges
chunks.text: A crown covers a damaged tooth and is made from porcelain, zirconia or gold. A bridge replaces one or more missing teeth using crowns on the teeth either side. Both usually take two appointments separated by about two weeks while a temporary is fitted. Crowns are rarely covered by insurance.

chunks.title: Root Canal Treatment
chunks.text: A root canal removes infected tissue from inside a tooth. It is normally completed in one or two visits under local anaesthetic and is not more painful than a filling. A crown is usually placed afterwards to protect the weakened tooth. It is often cheaper than extracting the tooth and replacing it with an implant.

chunks.title: Wisdom Teeth
chunks.text: Wisdom teeth are the third molars at the back of the mouth. We take digital X-rays to assess them. Impacted wisdom teeth that cause pain, infection or damage are removed surgically, usually by referral to an oral surgeon. Healthy wisdom teeth without symptoms are monitored rather than removed.

chunks.title: Checkups and Cleanings
chunks.text: A routine checkup and cleaning takes about 45 minutes and is recommended every six months. It includes a full mouth examination, a scale and polish and, where needed, small X-rays. Children and patients with gum disease are usually seen more often. Checkups are covered by most plans including Delta Dental, Cigna and MetLife.

chunks.title: Fluoride, Sealants and Cavity Prevention
chunks.text: Sealants are a thin protective coating applied to the chewing surfaces of back teeth and are recommended for children and teenagers. They usually last three to five years and are quick to apply. Adults at high risk of decay can have them too. Most insurance plans cover sealants on permanent molars.

chunks.title: Braces and Orthodontics
chunks.text: Braces, clear aligners and retainers are handled by an orthodontist, not by this practice. We can provide a referral and share your records and X-rays. Treatment typically takes 18 to 24 months and is rarely covered by dental insurance, though a limited amount is often available for under-18s.

chunks.title: Dentures
chunks.text: Full and partial dentures replace missing teeth. New dentures require several appointments for impressions, a wax try-in and fitting, then a follow-up adjustment. Adjustments in the first weeks are normal and expected. Patients who have had teeth removed should wait about three months before final dentures.

chunks.title: Night Guards and Teeth Grinding
chunks.text: A night guard is a custom-made splint worn overnight for people who grind their teeth or suffer from bruxism. Symptoms include a sore jaw on waking, flattened tooth edges and headaches. It is made from impressions taken in the office and usually takes two weeks to arrive from the lab.

chunks.title: Sports Mouthguards
chunks.text: A custom sports mouthguard protects teeth during contact sport and is recommended for anyone playing football, hockey, rugby or boxing. A boil-and-bite guard from a sports shop is less protective than a custom one. Custom guards take about two weeks and cost less than a single repair.

chunks.title: Gum Disease and Periodontics
chunks.text: Gum disease starts as gingivitis, with bleeding when brushing and bad breath, and can progress to periodontitis where the bone supporting the tooth is lost. Treatment is a deep clean below the gum line, usually over two or three appointments. Advanced cases are referred to a periodontist.

chunks.title: Tooth Sensitivity
chunks.text: Sensitivity to cold, hot or sweet usually means exposed root surface, worn enamel, a crack or gum recession. A desensitising toothpaste containing potassium nitrate usually helps after two weeks of daily use. Persistent sensitivity needs an examination, because it can indicate an underlying crack that will not resolve on its own.

chunks.title: Brushing and Flossing
chunks.text: Brush twice a day for two minutes with a soft brush and fluoride toothpaste. Floss or use interdental brushes once a day; the most common sites for decay are between the teeth and at the gumline. Replace a toothbrush every three months or when the bristles frayed.

chunks.title: Sugar and Diet
chunks.text: Frequent sugar exposure matters more than total sugar. Snacking on sweet or fizzy drinks between meals keeps the enamel in an acid attack for hours. Drinking water between meals and limiting sweets to mealtimes reduces decay noticeably. Smoking and smokeless tobacco substantially increase gum disease risk.

chunks.title: Dental Anxiety
chunks.text: Dental anxiety is common and the practice is set up for it. Tell the front desk when you book so the appointment can be longer and the first appointment can be a short orientation with no treatment. You can agree a hand signal to pause at any point. Tell us about it and we will adapt.

chunks.title: Sedation Options
chunks.text: Local anaesthetic is used for almost all treatment. Nitrous oxide, or laughing gas, is available for anxious patients and wears off within minutes. Oral or IV sedation is offered for longer or surgical appointments and requires you to be escorted home. You must not drive for 24 hours after IV sedation.

chunks.title: Payment Plans and Financing
chunks.text: Treatment over 500 dollars can be split into monthly instalments using a 12 month interest free plan, subject to a credit check. There is no interest and no early settlement fee. Plans are set up at the front desk and the first payment is taken on the day of treatment.

chunks.title: Billing Disputes and Refunds
chunks.text: An itemised statement is sent after every visit. If you believe a charge is wrong, contact the office within 30 days with the date of the visit and the item in question. Mistakes in our billing are corrected and refunded in full, usually within two weeks. Card refunds take a further three to five business days to appear.

chunks.title: Languages and Interpreters
chunks.text: English and Spanish are spoken at the practice, and a French speaking interpreter can be arranged with 48 hours notice. Written materials are available in Spanish, French and Chinese. For any other language we will book a professional interpreter at no cost to the patient.

chunks.title: Walk-ins and Same-Day Requests
chunks.text: Walk-ins are accepted for genuine emergencies only and are seen at the next available emergency slot, so there may be a wait. Non urgent walk-ins cannot be guaranteed a same day appointment. Calling ahead at 8:30am is the most reliable way to reach the first slot of the day.

chunks.title: Virtual Consultations
chunks.text: A virtual consultation is available for triage, post-operative review and treatment planning. It lasts about 20 minutes over a video call. A virtual visit cannot replace an examination that needs X-rays, and any treatment plan agreed is an estimate until you are seen in person.

chunks.title: Registration and Forms
chunks.text: New patient forms are sent by email or can be downloaded before the visit. Medical history, allergies and consent forms must be completed before treatment begins. Please bring your insurance card, photo identification and a list of current medications to the first appointment.

chunks.title: Prescription Refills
chunks.text: Repeat prescriptions for antibiotics and pain relief can be requested by phone or email and are collected at the front desk. Antibiotics are not issued without an examination. Controlled medications are never repeated by prescription alone and require an appointment.

chunks.title: Allergies and Medical Alerts
chunks.text: Tell us about latex, antibiotic, anaesthetic or metal allergies, and about any anticoagulant medication, before treatment. A medical alert in your medical history is enough; a letter from a doctor is not required. We will also note any condition that affects healing or bleeding.

chunks.title: Dental Care During Pregnancy
chunks.text: Routine checkups, cleanings and most treatments including X-rays are safe during pregnancy. Elective cosmetic work and whitening are deferred until after the birth. Second trimester appointments are the most comfortable. Always tell the dentist if you are pregnant, at any stage, including in the first weeks.

chunks.title: Second Opinions
chunks.text: You are entitled to a second opinion on any treatment plan. We will release your X-rays and records to the practitioner of your choice, and the consultation itself does not carry a charge. If you are unsure about a plan we recommend, ask for a written explanation before deciding.

chunks.title: Referring Friends and Family
chunks.text: You can refer a family member for general dentistry without paperwork and they will be seen as a new patient. Referring someone for orthodontics, oral surgery or implants requires a written referral because those services are provided by specialists. Existing patients can be seen as a courtesy walk-in for urgent pain.

chunks.title: Sending Documents and Photos
chunks.text: You can email a photo of a tooth or a referral letter to reception@northwinddental.example. Photos are useful for triage but never replace an examination. Please do not email payment card numbers or other sensitive personal data.

chunks.title: Dental Abscess and Infection
chunks.text: An abscess is a pocket of infection at the root of a tooth and causes constant throbbing pain, bad taste and sometimes facial swelling. It will not resolve on antibiotics alone because the source must be drained or the tooth treated. Treatment is urgent and should not be left longer than a few days.

chunks.title: Knocked-Out or Loose Tooth
chunks.text: A tooth knocked out in an adult can often be saved if it is replanted within about an hour. Hold it by the crown, not the root, rinse it in milk and put it back in the socket, or keep it in milk and come straight in. A tooth loosened by trauma should be seen the same day.
